title: Recursion, stack overflow, and tail calls
hook: Recursion, stack overflow, and tail calls shows up in everyday JavaScript and in senior interviews — this page explains what it is, why it matters, and how it behaves in the engine versus C# or TypeScript.

blocks.text: Recursion, stack overflow, and tail calls is a core concept in JavaScript (ECMAScript). At run time, the engine enforces behavior dynamically — there is no compile step unless you add TypeScript on top. This page explains the idea in plain English first, then shows small, explained examples you can run in the browser console or Node.js.

blocks.text: Senior interviews and production code both probe whether you understand Recursion, stack overflow, and tail calls beyond syntax memorization. Misunderstanding here leads to subtle bugs — wrong equality results, leaked memory, untyped JSON boundaries, or async ordering surprises. If you know C#, the comparison sections below help you transfer mental models instead of starting from zero.

blocks.body: Interviewers often ask "Recursion, stack overflow, and tail calls" as a follow-up to a coding exercise. They want mechanism and tradeoffs — not a one-line definition.
